# weka_ldap (Resource)

The cluster LDAP configuration. There is one per cluster; the id and the import id are `cluster`. Delete resets it.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "weka_ldap" "this" {
  enabled                    = true
  server_uri                 = "ldaps://ldap.example.com"
  base_dn                    = "DC=example,DC=com"
  user_object_class          = "user"
  user_id_attribute          = "sAMAccountName"
  group_object_class         = "group"
  group_id_attribute         = "cn"
  group_membership_attribute = "member"
  reader_username            = "reader@example.com"
  reader_password            = "placeholder"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `base_dn` (String) Base DN for LDAP searches.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the cluster uses LDAP for authentication.
- `group_id_attribute` (String) Attribute used as the group id.
- `group_membership_attribute` (String) Attribute listing the members of a group.
- `group_object_class` (String) Object class of a group entry.
- `reader_password` (String, Sensitive) Password for `reader_username`. GET /ldap does not return it; Terraform keeps the configured value.
- `reader_username` (String) Account the cluster uses to query the directory.
- `server_uri` (String) LDAP server URI (`[ldap://]hostname[:port]` or `ldaps://hostname[:port]`).
- `user_id_attribute` (String) Attribute used as the user id.
- `user_object_class` (String) Object class of a user entry.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Always `cluster`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import the cluster LDAP configuration.
terraform import weka_ldap.this cluster
```
